  on every frame of every clip: measured, face (0.12, 0.94, 0.33) with the
  trunk facing forward and down. The retarget's "A is not T" turn is found per
  bone from the direction to its mapped child, and the head has none — it took
  the NECK's. This rig binds like a zombie: the neck bone runs 130 degrees
  down and forward to a head craned back up it to face front (neck axis
  (0, -0.67, 0.74), head (0, 0.99, 0.11)), so turning the neck vertical took
  the head with it. `kind.alignLeaves` aligns a mapped leaf on its OWN axis —
  Blender's bone Y IS the bone, on both rigs — against the Mixamo bone's rest
  quaternion, which `ntar_moves.py` already writes. Opt-in, so nothing tuned
  moved. After: face (-0.2, -0.59, 0.78) in the crawl, forward in the run.
- **THE STANCE WAS FOUND IN THE PANE, NOT REASONED.** `tools/sheet.js` is the
  harness for it: `__pose(angles, hipY)` composes body-axis angles onto the
  crawl's first frame exactly as `poseRig` does and renders the result into a
  strip beside the owner's picture, with no reload per guess; `__sheet` strips
  a clip. The kneel (`CRAWL_STANCE`) is the trunk reared and twisted so the
  planted shoulder leads, the left hand on the sand, the right arm hanging
  bent, the right knee up under the chest with its foot down, the left shin
  back along the ground. **The arm and the leg were GRID-SEARCHED**: 1,512
  renders at four pixels each in 2.4 s, minimising the hand's height off the
  sand with its forward reach bounded — because a body-axis rotation on a
  forearm that happens to lie along X moves the hand in Z and not in Y, and
  no amount of reasoning about "bend the elbow" finds that. Measured: hand
  0.04 m over the sand, foot 0.01. The idles are the stance alive (breath,
  head jerks with holds, the jaw working, the weight rocking); the roar rears
  off the knee and DROPS ONTO ALL FOURS, which is what every blow is built on.
- **THE JAW IS A JOINT LIKE ANY OTHER.** `jaw: 'DEF-jaw_master'` in
  `CRAWL_JOINTS`; the bind is wide open, `right` negative closes it (rendered
  to know, not reasoned). The idles work it.
- **BIGGER IS A NUMBER THAT LEAKS INTO EVERY OTHER NUMBER.** `h` 1.92 -> 2.6
  scaled the model 1.374, and on all fours HIS FACE IS 1.43 m AHEAD OF HIS
  ORIGIN. Every stop and reach in the table is measured from the origin, so
  at stops of 1.9 his teeth were half a metre from the lens, 95 % of his
  contacts landed off the bottom of the frame, and the owner's picture would
  have been his back. The table is written round the FACE now: stops hold the
  origin at 2.7-3.0 (the face at about 1.1-1.5), reaches grew by the same 1.4,
  `hitR` 1.7 so the blade's sphere reaches a face that far forward, `body` 1.2.
  Measured pinned at 4.5 m: contacts 100 % on screen (was 5), median 0.73 m
  from the chest, 34 swings and 37 damage a minute, zero yaw spikes.
- **AND A TOKEN HOLDER SIX HUNDRED METRES AWAY NEVER GAVE IT BACK.** The
  harness's teleport crossed `MUT_Z` and woke the pack, the pack's swing never
  ended because nothing advances a unit that far away, and the release waited
  for the swing to end — so a beach mutant held the turn through a whole
  crawler fight and the crawler circled at two metres for ten seconds at a
  stretch (8.6 swings a minute, measured, and `bw.mutToken` — NOT
  `state().mutToken` — is how you see who has it). Past thirty metres a holder
  gives it back whatever it is doing.

And two harness lessons. **A knockback walks a pinned-nowhere player up the
beach**: forty metres of them put the harness player in the portal ring and
the dojo took him mid-sample (the camera read (2980, 801, 2979) and the
crawler ran to z 410 after him) — the crawler stands sixty metres past the
stones now, and a sampler that must not move pins the camera every tick. And
**`__sheetFor(unit)` before `__sheet`** — the tool is re-evaluated after every
reload and forgets whom it is for.

He runs one set-off in three (`gaits.run: ['crawl', 'crawl', 'run']`), a
hunched two-legged lope at 3.6 m/s clip speed played at the rate he moves,
the run cycle windowed to its eighteen frames because the importer pads it
with a held tail that hitched the loop; `fade` 0.22 on every crossfade; every
swing `ease`d; `chainMax` 2.

**THE SEA KEEP PUT YOU IN THE WATER, AND IT WAS THE ABDUCTION.** "I'm not
spawning on the dock when going to the sea keep, it's putting me here" — forty
metres off the pier at sea level, looking at the island. Traced with a setter
on `camera.position.x` that records a stack on any jump over five metres: on
the first frame after the cut `updateShrine` wrote x = 2973 (the hall's rim
clamp) and `updateKeep`'s own rim clamp then dragged the body back to the
island's edge. The hall was clamping because THE ABDUCTION HAD FIRED: moving
the saucer back behind the spawn put its trigger back to `z >= ABDUCT_Z`, and
every room this game has stands at POSITIVE z on purpose — the keep at 6000,
the tavern at 12000, the undercroft at 2400, the dojo at 6000 — because every
trigger on the walk was "z less than a line". The first turn on the pier the
beam took you. The trigger asks `!inRoom()` now and wants the beach's own x,
and the notes about "your Z alone" mean your Z on the beach. **When a fix to
one thing moves a comparison, walk the list of places that only ever agreed
with the old direction.**

**THE CRAWLER IS 3.1 m, HE RUNS AS OFTEN AS HE CRAWLS, AND YOU SEE HIS FACE.**
The owner's three: taller, bigger, scarier and more dangerous; the Mutant Run
sometimes and the crawl sometimes; and "I want you to see the creature's
face". The last one is the one worth writing down: every clip he fights with
is built on the crawl's first frame, and a crawl looks at the sand a stride
ahead, so what the player fought was the top of a skull. `kind.face` is a
constant lift of the neck and the head composed by the life layer through
every clip that is not an idle (the kneel already lifts it), and `face.hold`
keeps the eyes on you through a swing where the look used to drop to nothing
on the frame he committed — the aim yaws the model and the blow is swept on
the limbs, so the head is free to look. The table moved out again with his
height (the face is now 1.7 m ahead of the origin), the lunge takes two of
your four, `speedK` 1.6, `aggr` 3.4, chains three deep, and the run is drawn
one set-off in two.
Measured after, pinned at five metres over seventy seconds: **35.5 swings and
39 damage a minute, 100 % of contacts on screen, median claw 0.89 m from the
chest, his face toward the lens on 71 % of frames, zero yaw spikes** — and
the keep's pier holds the player for 300 frames after the cut where before
it lost him on the first.

**LONGER ARMS, A TRUNK CARRIED HIGH, AND HE GETS UP ON HIS HIND LEGS.** The
owner's three, in one message: front arms longer with the upper back and
neck up, "more human-like but still crawling"; a few standing attacks where
he rears and swings; and taller while crawling. What each cost:

- **A BONE SCALED CARRIES ITS SUBTREE, and a clip that carries no scale track
  lets it stand.** `bones: { 'DEF-upper_armL/R': 1.28 }` on the kind — the
  mutants' own trick — and every clip he plays is a retarget or an authored
  quaternion set, so nothing stamps a 1.0 back over it.
- **THE POSTURE IS COMPOSED, NOT RE-AUTHORED.** Every clip he fights with is
  built on the crawl's first frame, so raising the trunk is one offset in
  one place: `kind.posture` (waist, chest reared; the arms turned back down
  by nearly the same so the hands stay planted on their longer reach) goes
  through the life layer on the same gate as the face lift — every clip but
  the kneel, and not a swing marked `stand`. The numbers were GRID-SEARCHED
  in the pane: six crawl frames, the lowest hand held to 0.05 m in the sand,
  the highest shoulder preferred — 108 combinations, and the answer was the
  most reared trunk with the arms brought most under it (waist -0.40, chest
  -0.50, arms 0.70; shoulders 1.47 m over hips at 1.0). At the first guess
  (-0.20 / -0.30 / 0.50) the hands were 0.25 m under the sand.
- **AND THE FACE LIFT CAME DOWN WITH IT.** 0.62 rad on a level trunk was a
  face on you; on a reared one it was a face on the sky. 0.25.
- **THE STAND IS THE CRAWL'S FRAME STOOD UP** (`CRAWL_STAND`): hips lifted
  0.55, trunk 1.25 rad back, the legs grid-searched so the feet land under
  the hips — the right to 0.01 m, the left no nearer than 0.19, because the
  crawl folds it about an axis these keys do not turn — the head brought back
  down. Crown at 3.03 m, hands at 3.8 thrown up. `zRear` rises INTO the tell
  (the rise is the wind-up, the hang at the top is what you read) and slams
  both arms down; `zStandSwipe` rises with one arm cocked high and takes it
  across at chest height — MEASURED, because the first version crossed at
  2.7 m, over your head, and the fix was the arm's absolute angle at the
  contact key (-0.35 -> +0.55: on a trunk reared 1.25 rad an arm at zero
  already points up). Both take two of your four and both are slow enough to
  step. `stand` on the table entry is what keeps the posture off them.
- **AND `right` HAS TO EXIST BEFORE IT IS USED.** The posture block was first
  pasted above the line that derives the body's right axis and took the page
  down with a TDZ error on the first frame the life layer ran. Read the
  function's own order before inserting into it.
Measured after, pinned at five and a half metres over a minute: **26 swings
and 45 damage a minute** (slower and heavier than the crawl-only fight — the
standing blows are long and two of them take two of your four), every swing in
the draw used, contact medians 0.35–0.98 m with the bite back to 0.89 from
1.82 once `flat` dropped the posture for it, zero yaw spikes. A frozen frame of
the rear: fully upright over the lens, both claws coming down, jaws open.

**"HE'S PALMING YOU", AND THE CHEST STUCK UP: THE HUNCH IS THE RIG'S OWN
NECK.** The owner sent the artist's renders back
(cgtrader "Stylized Zmobie") with "less awkward, his hits don't look like
clawing, chest less weirdly stuck up, a natural hunch, taller looking down on
you, strong". Two things, and the second corrected the round before it:

- **A HAND NOBODY DRIVES IS FLAT, AND A FLAT HAND SLAPS.** Thirty finger
  bones, never keyed, so every swipe arrived palm first. `kind.claws` curls
  every phalanx about its own X all the time and harder through a blow, and
  THE SIGN IS DERIVED per bone (a curl shortens tip-to-wrist; each bone is
  turned both ways once at install and keeps the one that did) — the
  samurai's fist on a monster, and it needs no rendering to be right.
- **THE REFERENCE IS A HUMP, NOT AN ARCHED BACK.** Read off the renders: the
  shoulders are the highest point, the neck comes forward and DOWN out of the
  hump, and the face looks up from under the shoulder line. The round before
  reared the chest straight up (waist -0.40, chest -0.50), which is a man
  arching — the "weirdly stuck up" chest. `kind.posture` is a joint map now
  (any joint, body-axis angles, plus `lift` for the hips) and the fitted one
  lifts the lower back, curls the chest a shade forward, drops the neck 0.9
  ahead and cranes the head 0.9 back up — very nearly the rig's OWN bind
  pose, which is a zombie's neck and was the thing the retarget straightened
  out. The legs and arms were grid-searched over the crawl cycle for feet and
  the lowest hand on the sand, and the lift was swept: at 0.28 no arm reached
  the ground and hands 0.2 m up read as floating; 0.10 puts the lowest hand
  0.04 m into it with the chest at 1.46 m and the head at 1.20 (was 1.16 and
  0.75). The face lift went to zero with it: the crane does the looking.
Measured after, pinned at five and a half metres over sixty-six seconds: **29
swings and 41 damage a minute, 89 % of contacts on screen, his face toward
you 61 % of frames, head carried at 1.29 m in the crawl (the hump at your eye
line, the face looking up from under it, as the renders have it), zero yaw
spikes.** Frozen at a swipe's contact the forearm rakes across the lens with
the far hand's claws hooked in frame. Standing, he is three metres over you.

**THE CATACOMBS: THE SAND GIVES PAST THE STONES, AND THE MONSTER HUNTS YOU
UNDER IT.** The owner's brief in one message: a little after the portal the
ground caves in dramatically and you fall into wiz's "Catacombs Map"
(CC-BY-4.0, `assets/catacombs.glb`, `tools/undercroft_pack.py tavern` — exact,
142k triangles, 9.1 MB, NO `--scale`: the file already carries its own
centimetre root and a 0.01 on top made a 27 cm walk grid), landing in the crypt
room of the first screenshot; dark; the monster wandering the whole place
looking for you, his feet and claws heard scraping when he is near; attacking
only when he has you in sight; hard to kill; the way out the barred door of
the second screenshot with light through its window, onto the beach from a
door in the sand wall. `CAT_*`, the tavern's machinery on a third site.
What it cost, in the order it bit:

- **A ROOM IS FOUND, NOT NAMED.** The file has 744 nodes called `Object_N`.
  The rooms came out of the WALK GRID: flood the storeys by height into
  connected pieces, render each from inside (`tools/sheet.js` has
  `__loadGlb` / `__view` for it), and match the pictures. The crypt room is
  floor 0.34 at (5.6, -11.6); the barred door is the +x wall of the upper room
  at (8.84, 4.33, -14.4), flanked by torches at z -15.3 and -13.5 with skulls
  at its foot — the second screenshot exactly.
- **AND "YOUR Z ALONE" FIRES IN A ROOM AT POSITIVE Z — the keep's own lesson,
  the day after.** Not this time: the trigger is a BAND (`CAVE_Z` .. -7) on
  the beach with `!inRoom()`, and `caveDone` is on the save and inferred past
  it. The take is four beats on the wall clock (`updateCaveIn`): the shake and
  sand off the ground, the give (a crack and the camera falling under its
  own gravity with the black closing over it), the cut, the landing.
- **THE CLIFF CLAMP WAS STILL ON IN THE ROOM.** Every frame `update()` pulled
  `camera.position.x` to `CLIFF_BLOCK_X` — nine kilometres — and the hall cull
  then measured the room from the beach and HID it, and the room's walk put x
  back before anything drew, so the camera read as inside a room that had
  been switched off. Traced with a setter on `visible`: `cullWorldInHall`,
  under `update()`. `!inCat` joins the one list of places that are not this
  beach. (And a `bwSpan` frame that says "cannot access 'right' before
  initialization" is the life layer's TDZ from the round before, on the frame
  a page hidden to rAF finally drew him.)
- **THE HUNTER'S GRAPH IS THE STOREYED WALK AS NODES**, (cell, storey) with a
  hop over one missing cell (`catBuildGraph` / `catRoute`, breadth-first).
  Three filters were wrong before one was right: headroom 1.6 threw away the
  crypt room (this model's rooms are 1.5 m under the next slab — a catacomb;
  0.9, he crawls); a wall clearance of 0.28 m cut the graph into 229 pieces
  because its stairs and doorways are narrower than that (none — his body,
  not the graph, keeps him off walls); and "no roof" is the OUTSIDE of the
  model only when nothing stands over it in the same cell. Measured: 14,512
  nodes, one piece of 9,962 that reaches six of the seven rooms (the flooded
  level is the seventh).
- **A TARGET HE CAN REACH.** A random node anywhere was outside his piece often
  enough that, once down a stair into the water, every route failed and he
  stood there for good. `catFlood` from his own node, cached, and targets come
  from that.
- **AND THREE THINGS UNDID EVERY STRIDE.** The wall push at a cap of 0.06 a
  frame cancelled the follower's 4 cm step (a millimetre moved, a live route in
  hand); on a route he ignores the drawn faces and trusts the floor cells. The
  snap back to the last standable spot refused the one-cell gap the route
  hops; on a route he crosses it. And a stuck test on per-frame deltas never
  read as still while a clamp argued with the follower; it is NET progress
  over a second and a half now.
- **HE SEES YOU ON TWO EYE-LINES, ON YOUR STOREY.** `catSees`: inside thirty
  metres, a 72-degree cone (hearing inside six, and inside three whatever he
  faces), no drawn wall between his eye and yours at EITHER eye height (a
  tomb at chest height between you hides neither), and never a storey apart —
  at 2.6 m of slack he heard you through a floor and roared at the ceiling,
  and the fight AI, which is planar, then had him "in reach" of a player a
  storey up (`near` is false across a floor now). Lose him for six seconds
  from ten metres and he goes back to searching from where he last had you.
- **HIS FEET ARE CLAWS ON STONE.** `voice.scrape` routes his step through
  `sfxClawScrape`: a rasp swept down through a band, a click, a knock under
  it, panned by his bearing (`panTo`) and gone by twenty-six metres.
- **THE PANE HIDDEN TO rAF RUNS NO FRAMES**, and a hidden pane looked
  displayed to `tabs_context`: a reference tab opened beside it was enough.
  `bw.animate()` by hand drives a frame each; `document.hidden` is the truth.
  And a dev checkpoint left 14 m from him reloaded the page every nineteen
  seconds — `playerDied` — for a whole round of "nothing works".

Measured: he wanders 50 m in 22 s across three storeys, walks into the crypt
room, sees you and roars; in the room 9 swings and 12 damage in 14 s at 2.6 m
with his face on you 98 % of frames; the door puts you on the sand at
(12.6, -800) with the wall door 1.9 m to your right and the checkpoint written.
Health 80, poise 12, a guard of 0.28.

Two smaller ones from the last look. **You land where the picture was taken
from**, not in the middle of the room: `CAT_LAND` is (7.0, -12.5) facing the
green tomb, because the first spot put the sarcophagus at your back and the
first thing you saw of the crypt was a wall. And **a door swung -0.72 about Y
opens OUT over the beach**: a leaf built along +z swings to (sin, 0, cos) of
its yaw, and -x is seaward here, so the door in the sand wall stood across
the frame with the beach behind it; +0.72 puts it into the recess, where the
comment always said it was. Read a swing's sign off where the leaf ENDS UP.

**AND THEN THE CATACOMBS WERE TWICE THE SIZE, PITCH DARK, AND THE THING IN
THEM LIVED THERE.** The owner played it: everything too small to walk
through, he could not fit in the doors, the monster glitched through the
ground and was lit up like a lamp, and the room lagged all over. Seven
things, and the two that mattered most are both about a graph.

- **A ROOM IS SCALED AT THE PACKER, NOT IN THE GAME.** `tools/undercroft_pack.py
  tavern … --scale 2.2`. Measured on the first pack: rooms 1.5 m from floor
  to slab against a 1.88 m body, and corridors 0.6 m wide — that is a
  catacomb you crawl through sideways and it is exactly what "I couldn't fit
  in the doors" is. At 2.2 the rooms are 3.3 m and the doorways 1.3 to 2.
  Every number the game holds about the place is written `× CAT_SCALE`, so a
  spot measured in the old file is the same spot in the new one.
- **VERY DARK, WHICH IS A LEVEL AND A REACH.** The stone carries 0.03 of its
  own map (it was 0.085), the fog is 0.040 and near-black, and a torch is
  1.7 over 8.5 m rather than 2.6 over 11 — so a torch is a pool with dark
  either side of it and not a room light. What carries the place is the
  flames, the door's cold glow and what you are holding.
- **AND HE WAS LIT FOR A BEACH.** `emis` 0.10 with a cold Fresnel rim is the
  pack's night lift — a creature on open sand under a quarter moon is a hole
  in the dark without it — and in a room whose stone reads 3 it made him a
  pale animal visible across the whole hall. Measured by rendering him and
  then hiding him and diffing the frame: at 3 m he covers 6.3 % of it at a
  mean of 9.8 against the room's 3.2, which is a dark shape you can just
  make out. `emis` 0.022, the rim a third of what it was.
- **A FLOOR LOOKUP SEARCHES DOWNWARD, WHICH IS HOW HE WENT THROUGH THE
  GROUND.** Standing over a stair well or a hole in a vault, `keepFloorAt`
  answers with the storey BELOW — and the follow eased him into it at three
  metres a second. `catStand` is the one door now: a floor more than a
  stride under him is not his floor, he holds the last one he stood on, and
  if he holds it for most of a second he is put back on the nearest node at
  that height and his route dropped. Measured over ninety seconds of
  roaming: never more than 0.27 m under a floor, and 1 % of frames with
  nothing under him at all.
- **"I LAGGED ALL OVER THIS ROOM" WAS THE ROUTE, AND IT WAS THREE FAULTS IN
  ONE SEARCH.** Measured: 9.6 ms a route with the chase asking for one every
  0.4 s. (1) It was a BREADTH-FIRST search over 53,145 nodes, which visits
  every one of them before it gives up — A* with the straight-line distance
  finds a path in a tenth of a millisecond. (2) The reachable set was an
  ARRAY and `Array.includes` over 35,324 ids was asked every time he chose
  somewhere to go; it is a mask. (3) A node every 0.2 m is nine times the
  graph a crawling animal needs — at 0.6 m it is 5,887 nodes and the build
  is 112 ms rather than 275.
- **AND A WEIGHTED HEURISTIC IS INCONSISTENT, SO A* MUST CLOSE WHAT IT HAS
  EXPANDED.** This is the one that took the longest to see, because the
  symptom lies: routes to nodes his OWN FLOOD had just proved reachable came
  back refused, eleven in twenty, at seven milliseconds each. Every one of
  them had popped 14,001 entries — the cap — on a graph of 5,887 nodes,
  because a node whose cost improves after it has been popped gets expanded
  again, and with a 1.3 weight that cascades. A closed stamp ends it: 30 of
  30 routes, median 0.9 ms, worst 2.1. **If a search fails on something you
  can prove is reachable, count its expansions before you touch anything
  else.**
- **AND A SPOT RESOLVES TO A NODE ON THE STOREY YOU MEANT.** Two rooms stack
  at the same (x, z) all over this place, so `catNodeAt` can answer with the
  floor above or below the one a target was taken from — and the route was
  then refused as unreachable by the very flood that produced it. It takes
  the reach mask and prefers a node inside it.

**AND HIS MIND IS AMNESIA'S NOW: HE LIVES HERE, AND YOU ARE IN THE WAY.**
Six modes. ROAM — he picks a bone pile to eat at (found by bucketing the
skull mesh's own vertices, not typed), a room to stand in, or somewhere
near where you happen to be, and goes there crawling, one leg in three up
on his hind legs. ACT — he eats, sits back on his haunches, stands and
looks about where the roof allows, or crouches and listens, five to fifteen
seconds, facing one way, which is how you get past him. INVESTIGATE — your
sprint carries 24 m, your walk 11, a crouch 5, and a landing, a swing and a
blade on stone say so where they happen (`catNoiseAt`); he comes and
searches. STALK — the owner's own brief: from across a room he does NOT
charge, he goes to a corner that can see you and puts his face round it
(`catPeekSpot`: a node 9 to 22 m off that can see your eye AND where a step
to one side of it cannot, which is what a corner IS, measured rather than
authored), and holds there. What turns that into a fight is YOU looking at
him — the middle of your screen, not the edge of it. FLEE — under a third
of his health, once a fight, he breaks off, runs for somewhere at least 22 m
from you, mends about a point a second, and comes back; `blooded` is set, so
the second time he does not peek, he simply comes. CHASE — the fight.

- **AND A MODE IS NOT RE-ENTERED BY THE THING THAT STARTED IT.** The sight
  check runs six times a second and set the mode to `stalk` again on every
  one of them, which reset the clock that ends a stalk and threw away the
  spot he was walking to: traced, he stood fourteen metres off doing nothing
  for ten seconds. A sight that arrives while he is already stalking only
  refreshes where he thinks you are.
- **AND "IS THE LINE OPEN" IS THE WHOLE LINE, NOT THE NEXT TWO METRES.** The
  chase dropped its route whenever the nearest 2.2 m looked clear, then walked
  into a wall three metres on, where the new segment clamp held him — a route
  made and thrown away four times a second at twelve metres. It asks as far
  as he can see now, and he closed 16 m to 5.2.
- **AND HE MAY NOT PASS THROUGH A WALL BETWEEN FRAMES** — the player's own
  rule, and the whole of "he clipped through the map running": the chase
  drove him at drawn stone at seven metres a second against a push that
  corrected 1.5 cm a frame. The frame's movement is a segment at his hip and
  his shoulder, and a frame that crossed a face is reverted.
- **AND A CORNER HE WATCHES FROM IS FURTHER OFF THAN THE RANGE AT WHICH HE
  COMES.** At five metres the peek spot was already inside the distance that
  turns a stalk into a charge, so he arrived and charged on the same frame
  and there was no peek at all.
- **AND A THING THAT REARS UP NEEDS A ROOF TO REAR UNDER.** His two standing
  blows put his hands 3.8 m up; a catacomb's rooms are 3.3. They are out of
  the draw wherever the storey he is on has less than 4.3 m over it.

Measured at the end. **The player's own walk floods 12,404 cells from the
landing with a standing body and reaches the barred door to within 0.1 m.**
Routes: 30 of 30, median 0.9 ms. **Fourteen seconds of live fighting with
NO frame over 16 ms** (before: 9.6 ms of routing several times a second).
The fight is 30 swings and 39 damage a minute at 2.5 m, against the Dealer's
48 and 40. He roams 140 m in ninety seconds. Hurt to 18 of 80 he breaks off,
mends to 40 and comes back. And the dev-mode trap caught a whole round of
measurement again: **`devMode` turns a creature's swinging off outright**, so
a fight sampled with it on reads zero swings and a creature standing still.

**AND THEN HE GOT A HOME, A GRAB, AND NO DEATH.** Seven things on the
owner's list, and the useful ones are the three that change what the
encounter IS rather than how it looks.

- **DEV MODE SURVIVES A RELOAD THE GAME ITSELF ASKED FOR.** "No deaths, no
  cutscenes" is what you are testing WITH, and every death and every
  restart-from-checkpoint reloads the page — so it came back off and the
  takes you had just skipped played again. It rides in `sessionStorage`,
  written by `reloadInto` and consumed at boot, which a new tab does not
  have: a game still always starts as a game. And the cave-in is a take, so
  in dev mode it does not play one — it still puts you in the room.
  Measured: `caveBusy` never goes true and you are in the catacombs.
- **HE DOES NOT DIE, HE GOES DOWN.** A catacomb with a corpse in it is a
  catacomb you have finished, and the whole of the fear down there is that
  it is his and you are in it. `kind.undying` intercepts `killMutant`: the
  blow still lands, still throws him, still reads as a kill — and he lies
  where he fell with the death clip held on its last frame for forty to
  sixty seconds, then the same clip runs BACKWARDS, which is a body rocking
  back onto its hands, and he is up with two thirds of his health and a
  roar. Measured: down 43 s, up at 53 of 80, straight into a stalk.
- **AND HE TAKES YOU IF YOU ARE NOT LOOKING.** `catCanGrab` wants him inside
  2.9 m, on your storey, and your eyes off him for a second and a half
  (`catSeenAt`, stamped six times a second the same way his own sight is) —
  and then it is not a swing, it is a TAKE: up off your feet with his face
  in yours, screaming, a point gone, and thrown back down on the spot you
  were standing. It costs your footing and the thing you were about to do
  and it leaves you playing, which is worth more than a death screen. It
  runs on the wall clock beside the cave-in and the door, the camera is
  turned and never moved, and `catGrabT >= 0` is in `frozen()`.
- **AND A TAKE SETS THE POSE; IT DOES NOT ASK FOR IT.** `mutPlay` crossfades,
  which is right for a fight and wrong for a scripted beat: measured
  mid-grab, the grab clip sat at weight 0 with the crawl still at 1 and what
  played was the crawl. Setting the weight explicitly was not enough either
  — BOTH then read 1, because an action the mixer has already bound goes on
  contributing until something zeroes it. Every other action is stopped,
  zeroed AND disabled. (`stopAllAction` is the one thing that must not be
  used here: it restores every bound property, which is the bind pose — the
  severed limb's own bug.) And the take OWNS him: the fight's own `mutAnim`
  was picking a gait over the top of it.
- **HE MOVES LIKE HE KNOWS THE PLACE, WHICH IS A STRING-PULL.** A route over
  a grid is a staircase of little turns — cell, cell, cell — and what that
  reads as is a thing feeling its way along a wall. `catSmooth` drops any
  waypoint whose neighbours can see each other (`catLineOpen`: the drawn
  faces at his hip and his shoulder, the floor under every stride, and the
  headroom), so what is left is the long runs a thing that lives here would
  take and the turns are only where the walls actually turn. Measured: legs
  went from 0.6 m to 3.0–4.3, a 74 m route from about 120 waypoints to 26.
- **AND HE STALKS A GREAT DEAL MORE.** He goes to a corner from eight metres
  out rather than eleven; a stalk is THREE corners, each nearer than the
  last, rather than a clock; a peek is held five to eleven seconds; losing
  you in a fight sends him back to watching half the time rather than always
  searching; and `blooded` — which is what makes him charge instead of peek
  — lapses after forty seconds, so the second half of a long visit is not
  all fighting.
- **AND THE BONES ARE THE THING THAT TELLS YOU ABOUT NOISE.** His hearing has
  been in the game since he went in — a sprint carries 24 m, a walk 11, a
  crouch 5 — and nothing ever told the player so. The floor of a catacomb is
  bones: run through a pile of them (the piles the game already finds by
  bucketing the skull mesh's own vertices) and it is a dry clatter with no
  body under it, a puff of dust, and a noise that carries twenty-six metres.
  It is the one thing down there that makes where you walk a decision.
- **AND SOMETHING IN THE AIR.** Two `Points` batches and one draw each: motes
  that are POSITIONS rather than particles — a slow wander round a fixed
  offset from wherever you are standing, so the air is always full and
  nothing is ever born or dies — and dust, a pool that recycles, thrown
  where something happened: his feet on the stone within sixteen metres, a
  pile of bones kicked through.

**"I NEVER SAW HIM THE PAST 2 TIMES I PLAYED" WAS THREE THINGS, AND THE
FIRST IS THE OLDEST MISTAKE IN THIS FILE.** The owner walked the catacombs
twice and the thing that lives in them never once crossed his path. Measured
with the player standing still in the door room for three minutes: he came
within **1.5 m** and never saw them, and never counted as being in that room
at all. Both readings are the same fact — **a distance with the y left out is
not a distance.** Two rooms stack at the same (x, z) all over this place and
he was ten metres BELOW, which his own senses already refuse (`catSees` will
not see through a storey). His convergence targets are drawn from nodes on
YOUR OWN FLOOR now (within 1.8 m of your feet), and the prowl mostly is too.

- **AND A BEAM OF LIGHT IS NOT A WALL.** "Let me run up to the door, I got
  stuck here": the door's decorative light shaft is a `PlaneGeometry` hung
  3.3 m out from the leaf, and `buildKeepWalls` reads every drawn face — so
  the walk stopped the player exactly one body radius in front of a sheet of
  light. It, the glow and the hit proxy carry `bwGhost` (drawn, never walked
  into), which the tavern's tables already needed. Measured: a 3.56 m gap
  became -0.03.
- **AND A WALL IS SLID ALONG, NOT STOPPED AT** — the player's own rule and
  the church's, which his own clamp never got. A frame whose movement crossed
  drawn stone was reverted WHOLE, and a revert is standing still; with a
  route nothing above ever asks to redraw, that is a creature parked for
  good. Traced with the player in one room: **seventy-five seconds held at
  25.9 m with a live eight-waypoint path in his hands and the revert firing
  on half the frames.** Whichever ONE AXIS of the step is clear is kept.
- **AND A STALK THAT IS NOT GETTING ANYWHERE IS NOT A STALK.** Net progress
  over five seconds; under a metre of it drops the route and asks for another
  corner, and three goes is all he gets before he simply comes. The backstop
  that ended a stalk was 95 s, which is a minute and a half of a boss
  standing still — 45.

Measured after, real time, player standing at the landing and the creature
parked 44.6 m away on another storey: he closes to **5.2 m and charges at
48 s**, against never. And the room the way out is in is one of his — the
nodes within twelve metres of the door, found off the door rather than typed,
and he goes there about a quarter of the times he picks an errand.

Three measurement traps paid for on the way. **Dev mode turns a creature's
swinging off outright**, so a creature standing at its ring doing nothing is
what dev mode looks like and not a bug (`atk: -1`, `cool: 0`, the idle
playing). **A page that has not been reloaded is the old module** — the door
spots read zero for a whole round because the graph in the tab had been built
before the code that fills them existed. And `u.path` on this follower is
**LOCAL x/z with a world f**, against `u.pathO`; printing a waypoint against
the room's origin subtracts it twice and every distance comes out in the
thousands.

**THE GRAB IS OUT, AND WHAT IT TAUGHT IS THAT NOTHING MAY LEAVE A RIG
UNBOUND.** "Take out the grab, it's bad, he T-posed right after it." He did,
and the reason is general enough to be worth the note even though the beat
is deleted: a TAKE owns the mixer while it runs — every other action
stopped, zeroed AND disabled, because `stop()` alone leaves an action
contributing and the crawl and the grab then averaged into one pose — and
what handed the body back was `u.cur = null` plus a fresh draw. **A frame on
which no action carries weight is a frame drawn in the BIND pose**, and this
rig binds standing in an A. `catBound` is the net and it hangs off
`catStand`, which every branch the creature has already calls: if nothing at
all is stamping him, the idle is, on the same frame. Measured by doing to
him exactly what the grab did — every clip stopped, zeroed and disabled —
and stepping one frame: he comes back on the idle and carries on into a
stalk with the crawl playing. The same line went out of the undying rise,
which cleared `u.cur` for no gain: a scripted beat has to blend OUT of its
last pose, which is what the knockdown does and is the shape to copy if a
grab ever comes back.

**AND THE HORDE'S TAKE PLAYED ON EVERY RESTORE FROM THE TUNNEL.** The pack
at the dock has had "a trigger you have already crossed does not fire again"
since the day the checkpoint went in; the three past the pavilion never got
it, and the cave's own save is written THIRTY METRES past them — so loading
it opened with the cutscene, at a stretch of sand whose creatures are
behind you. (Dev mode skips that take on the walk and cannot skip one that
fires on the frame the save is read.) `beginRestore` marks it crossed and
leaves them asleep on their marks. Measured from the cave's spot, dev mode
on and off: `mutPhase` 2, `mutCut` false, the field of view untouched.

**AND A CHECKPOINT AT THE TOP OF THE HOIST, WHICH IS A SAVE IN A ROOM.**
Everything past it — the terrace, the keep's door, the tavern, the two men
in it — is behind a sail, a walk round an island and a ride, and none of it
is worth doing twice. It is written the moment the car arrives with you ON
it (inside `keepLiftBox` and standing at its deck), once a game.

**A SAVE MADE IN A ROOM IS NOT A POSITION ON THE BEACH.** Every checkpoint
before this one was written on the sand, so `pos` was a place; this one is
eight kilometres out on an island that is not fetched, not built and not
entered when the save is read. Handed straight to the camera it is a body
on the beach's own clamps, dragged back to the sand on the first frame. The
save carries `room` now, and a restore that reads `keep` HOLDS THE POSITION
— the black card up, `loadKeep`, and `updateKeepRestore` on the wall clock
until `keepReady` — then `placeInKeep`, the hoist parked at the top where
you left it, and you set down on the spot it was written at. It is the
sail's own honest failure: if the island never comes, the black stays.
Measured: the save reads `room: "keep"` at (-6002.5, 817.85, 6014.9), and a
reload into it comes up standing on the car at the terrace facing the
studded door with "E Lower the hoist" under the crosshair.

**THE SAMURAI STOOD THERE BECAUSE A CREATURE'S FEET ARE NOT AN EYE MINUS A
BODY.** "He keeps getting stuck in place" and "he stops attacking even when
you get close" are one line. `pushOutOfDojo(p, r, feet)` is the PLAYER's call
and its `feet` is optional, falling back to `p.y - playerEye()`; `mutClampX`
called it with two arguments, and a mutant's group already sits on the floor
— so the wall band it tested ran from 1.14 m UNDER the boards to 0.05 m over
them and caught the risers of the step he was standing on. Measured: the
chase moved him 0.10 m toward the player and this put him back 0.10 m, on
every frame. He stood 3.04 m away for 38 of 40 seconds and threw NOT ONE
SWING — and every diagnosis that starts "the AI has stopped deciding to
attack" is wrong, because he was never allowed to close. After: 40.5 swings
and 54 damage a minute, median range 1.23 m, worst stall 1.13 s (the Dealer
is 48 and 40). **An optional argument with a player-shaped default is a trap
the day a creature calls it.**

**AND A CORPSE'S GROUND IS A LOOKUP PER PARTICLE — the gibs' rule, on a
ragdoll.** `updateMutRagdoll` took ONE floor, at the spot the creature died,
and gave it to all 22 particles. On a beach, a hall and a bunker floor that
is the same number everywhere and the error cannot show; the courtyard has a
step in it. Measured: killed on the veranda at 800.58 the body slid four
metres onto the yard at 800.20 and came to rest with its lowest joint 0.45 m
in the air. Each joint asks what is under ITSELF now, and off the grid it
keeps the body's own floor so a part thrown past the edge of a room still has
something to land on. Two things came with it: a floor made of cells is not
LEVEL across a two-metre body, so the constraints turn the disagreement into
a permanent millimetre of jitter and at the sand's 1e-7 the corpse was solved
for ever — a room gets the surf's own looser threshold; and at rest the body
now lies ACROSS the step with a 0.56 m spread of floors under it, which is
what a body draped over a step should do. Measured after: 22 parts, worst
constraint 1.012, asleep at 2.15 s, hips 0.28 m over the floor they are
actually over.

**AND THE ROOM'S MEMORY IS SEEDED BY THE THING THAT PUTS YOU IN IT.** The
catch that stops the player falling out of the courtyard reads
`dojoLastFloor`, and nothing set that until a frame had already come back
with a floor. The very first frame in the room is always a bad one —
`placeInDojo` calls `warmDojo()` three lines up, which renders the whole
courtyard several times, so the frame after it is most of a second long and
one step of gravity at that dt puts the feet ten metres under the boards.
Measured: the camera went 801.9 → 301 → 171 and kept going at 130 m/s.
`placeInDojo` knows where it is standing you; it says so.

**AND A DROP THAT ALWAYS POINTS DOWN DOES NOT NEED A RAYCASTER.**
`buildDojoBlocks` cast `Raycaster.intersectObject(dojoWorld, true)` straight
down once per column and once per stone, and three has no spatial index:
measured with a counter, **470 rays at 1.93 ms each — 909 ms of a 978 ms
`dojo blocks` span, inside a 1292 ms `courtyard.glb` freeze** on the frame
the room lands, which is the hitch on the walk up to the portal. The room's
43,571 triangles go into a one-metre (x, z) grid ONCE and a drop is then a
point-in-triangle over the handful in one cell: **978 → 73 ms, and
`courtyard.glb` 1292 → 154.** Two things it has to keep or the rubble
reseats itself — the material's SIDE (three culls back faces, so a downward
ray never meets the underside of a roof) and the old filter's rejects — and
the way to prove it is to run both against each other: **3200 of 3200 sample
points agree, 1280 of them real hits, zero disagreements.** The first guess
was that the build was quadratic because the ray also tested the stones it
was adding; that was real, and worth 23 ms of 1204. **Count the rays before
blaming their targets.**

**AND THE PREVIEW PANE HIDES ITSELF ON EVERY TOOL CALL, WHICH STOPS rAF
DEAD.** Three separate measurements this session read "the creature never
moves" and "the take never finishes" when what was actually true was
`document.hidden` and zero frames. Worse, a screenshot does NOT flush the
real rAF queue, and once the loop's callback is sitting in it the loop is
unrecoverable — a pump that stubs `requestAnimationFrame` cannot get it back.
`__bw.step(dt)` runs the real `update()` and needs no frame loop at all, and
the wall-clock work `animateFrame` does is already mirrored into it. **Drive
the game with `step`; check `document.hidden` before believing any measured
zero.** (And a screenshot taken after setting an overlay's `src` shows the
PREVIOUS frame, so a contact sheet needs a call of its own — this file has
said so before and it cost an hour again.)

**THE FOUNTAIN'S POOL WAS A HOLE IN THE FLAGSTONES, AND ITS WATER WAS A LADDER
OF PILLS.** Rendered at last — four angles, in game, at the retro scale — and
both halves of it were wrong in ways that are already written down here:

- **METALNESS IS A TRAP, THE FIFTH TIME, AND THIS TIME ON WATER.** The pool
  shipped at `roughness 0.08, metalness 0.30`, which is a polished near-metal:
  no diffuse term, no environment map in this game, so it can only show what a
  light reflects straight back at the eye. It rendered as a flat BLACK DISC
  with a hard rim and not one of the caustics drawn for it was visible
  anywhere on it. Dark is not black — water at night is a DIELECTRIC that
  keeps its diffuse, takes a broad soft sheen off the moon rather than a
  pinpoint, and lets the caustics and the basin floor under it do the rest.
  `metalness 0, roughness 0.42`, and the opacity comes down with it, because
  the one thing that separates water from a lid is seeing the stone through
  it. (The tunnel's channel is the deliberate exception and says so: a MIRROR
  of a specific light has no diffuse to lose.)
- **AND A VEIL THAT STOPS AT A HAND'S WIDTH LEAVES THE DROPS TO DO THE
  FALLING.** Each tier's sheet was capped at 0.30 m against a bottom tier
  that falls a full metre, so sixty-eight little boxes carried the rest —
  which at 16 mm across is eight pixels on screen, a white BAR, and
  sixty-eight of them is a ladder standing round the fountain. The sheet
  falls the whole way now and the drops are a third as many at half the
  width: they are the sparkle coming off it, not the thing itself.
- **AND WHAT MADE A FULL-HEIGHT TUBE A DRUM WAS NEVER ITS LENGTH, IT IS ITS
  TWO HARD CIRCULAR EDGES** — so the answer is the alpha, not the geometry.
  The first pass faded in at the top and out at the bottom, which puts the
  strongest part of the sheet halfway down and holds it at FULL alpha across
  the whole middle: a milky drum with the carving invisible behind it, the
  same drum wearing the opposite coat. Water leaves a brim as a skin and then
  ACCELERATES, and a sheet that accelerates gets thinner — it peaks just
  under the lip and tapers all the way down, so the pedestal reads through
  the bottom half.
- **AND A DISC OF WATER HAS NO SCALE.** Nine lily pads float in the ring
  outside the bottom tier's overhang, which is the only part of the pool
  anyone sees from standing height. A pad is a circle with a WEDGE out of it
  (`CircleGeometry`'s `thetaLength`) — the notch is the whole silhouette, and
  without it they are coins — one InstancedMesh with a tone per pad
  (`setColorAt`), because a dozen identical greens read as one printed
  pattern. They drift, because a pool fed from the middle turns.

**AND AN OVERSIZED TOOL RESULT IS SAVED TO A FILE, WHICH IS HOW A PICTURE GETS
OUT OF THE PANE.** Screenshots of the preview only capture when the pane is
displayed, it re-hides on every tool call, and an overlay `<img>` at the top
of the z-order does not composite while it is hidden — three rounds of this
session were judged on a frame from two calls earlier. The way that works:
render the sheet into a 2D canvas in ONE call (`drawImage` off the WebGL
canvas must be in the same task — no `preserveDrawingBuffer`), `toDataURL` it,
and return the bare base64. It blows the result limit, the harness writes it
to disk, and `base64.b64decode` in a shell turns it into a real .jpg that can
be read and sent to the owner — for no token cost at all, and he gets a file
rather than a screenshot of a pane.

**AND THE LILY PADS WERE NOT THE THING THAT WAS FLOATING.** "The lily pads are
floating above the water" — measured, a pad sits **3.4 mm** over the pool disc,
which is exactly where a pad should be. What was floating was THE WATER.
`FOUNT_POOL_Y` was typed as 0.26; the courtyard scan's own basin has its floor
at **0.127 and its rim topping out at 0.205**, so the disc hung five
centimetres ABOVE THE RIM of the thing it is supposed to be inside — a plate of
water over the whole basin. It is dark and two thirds transparent, so what the
eye took for the bottom was the stone thirteen centimetres below it, and the
pads read as hovering that thirteen centimetres.

The fountain's stone is the SCAN'S, so the only honest source for a water line
is the model. `buildFountain` reads it now: `dojoDropY` (already a one-metre
triangle grid, so this is a few dozen lookups and not one raycast) takes the
floor out in the ring past the bottom tier's overhang, walks outward until the
stone lifts to find the inner face of the rim, and the water goes a few
centimetres over the floor and safely under the rim — 0.143, a 1.65 cm depth,
with the disc's radius cut to 0.73 so its edge dies behind the rim instead of
crossing it. The bottom tier's `to` is resolved against it as well, or the
fall ends in the air above the water. Repack the courtyard and all of it still
lands in the basin. **A height typed for a hand-built prop is a guess the day
that prop is standing in somebody else's mesh.**

**AND THEN THE WHOLE GAME WAS PROFILED AGAIN, ROOM BY ROOM.** The owner's
word: a lot has been added, make it run smooth, only improve. The method is
the one this file already carries — put the camera at a station, let the
far-cull run, then hide each top-level scene child in turn and read
`renderer.info.render.calls` back — and the instrument that keeps it honest
is the PIXEL DIFF: render the frame twice, once with the cull and once with
everything it hid put back, and count the pixels that differ. Every cut
below measures **0.00 % of the frame**.

- **FIVE HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE MESHES WERE DRAWN INSIDE A SEALED ROOM FORTY
  METRES UNDER THE SAND.** The hatch's home is hidden while you are not in
  it and has been since it went in — but everything it was FURNISHED with
  was added to the scene beside it rather than under it: the props, the
  bottles, the desk, the camera, the case, the Dealer. Measured standing on
  the beach at z = -180: twenty-six top-level groups, every one of them
  visible, a third of the frame's draw calls. `bunkerTenantry` is the hall's
  own hide inverted, and who lives in the room is a question about WHERE A
  THING IS — the room's own box, asked when you leave — so nothing has to be
  registered at the twenty places these are made. Measured: **-149 draw
  calls at z = -240, and a pixel diff of zero standing on the hatch looking
  straight down at it.**
- **AND THE BEACH WAS DRAWN FROM INSIDE IT.** The same rule the other way,
  which every room three thousand metres out has had since the saucer went
  in and the one forty metres down never got, because the hall's test is a
  DISTANCE and this room is close. Measured on the control room's floor:
  **272 draw calls and 287k triangles became 128 and 67k.**
- **A PACKED SCAN IS ALL NAMES, SO `bakeStatic` HAD NEVER LOOKED AT ONE.**
  `Object_413` is not somebody holding a mesh, it is the exporter counting.
  The catacombs are 747 meshes in a handful of materials: measured standing
  in the crypt, **257 draw calls of which the room was 243** — the most
  expensive thing in the game. Merged by material in world space (so the
  grime shader, the wall index and every floor probe see the same
  triangles): **27**. The walk is unchanged — flooded from the landing it
  reaches 16,881 cells and comes within 0.78 m of the barred door.
- **AND THE TAVERN HALL WAS TWO HUNDRED AND TWENTY OF THEM.** 221 meshes,
  nineteen materials, twenty thousand triangles — ninety triangles a draw.
  It is the DEFAULT bake, so the eighteen meshes the module holds by name
  and the sixty-three `bwGhost` tables and chairs are left exactly where
  they are, and it runs LAST, after the tables have been lifted out of the
  mesh, the chairs built, the crates copied and the door cut. **354 → 216**,
  and the hall still floods to its own walls.
- **AND A UNIT BIGGER THAN THE SKYLINE WAS EXEMPTED WHEN IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN
  SPLIT.** `cullBeyondFog` measures a unit's reach from its own ORIGIN, and
  for a catch-all group parked at (0, 0, 0) that is the distance to the far
  side of the beach: measured, a group of fifty-one meshes whose children run
  from z = -35 to z = -640 reported a reach of 652 and was therefore never
  culled, anywhere, for the whole walk. A group is not a landform because its
  contents are spread out — it is asked about its CHILDREN instead, and only
  a single drawn mesh genuinely bigger than `SKYLINE_R` keeps the exemption.
  Measured as an A/B in one page, the same frame with the cull and with
  everything it hid restored:

| z | with | without | saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 83 | 102 | 19 |
| -180 | 264 | 321 | 57 |
| -240 | 269 | 404 | 135 |
| -420 | 148 | 359 | 211 |
| -700 | 98 | 393 | 295 |

  and 100–290k triangles with it. Thirteen stations, forward and backward,
  pixel diff **0.000–0.003 %**.

**AND WHAT WAS MEASURED AND LEFT ALONE IS WORTH WRITING DOWN TOO.** The
undercroft draws eleven calls from anywhere inside it and the sea keep
twenty-four: both were merged by their packer and there is nothing there to
win. The wreck is ninety meshes and twenty-four materials, and the biggest
mergeable run of twenty-two sits under a `noBake` group somebody set on
purpose — 93 draw calls is what the game's biggest set piece costs inside
the fog's own 170 m, and that is the design. And the walk is not CPU-bound
at all: `update()` is **0.41 ms** a frame and the render call 0.64–1.10 ms,
measured at four stations. What these cuts buy is the Windows frame, where
a draw call is a validated D3D11 call — which is the whole reason this file
counts draws and not triangles.

**AND A STATION SWEEP MUST NOT CROSS A TRIGGER.** Teleporting down the beach
past `CAVE_Z` puts you in the catacombs (in dev mode, without even a take),
and every station after it reads sixteen draw calls with the world culled
behind you — half an hour of this round was spent on numbers measured from
inside a room. Sweep to -750 and no further, or set `caveDone` first. And a
frame's `renderer.info` belongs to the LAST render call: `autoReset` is on,
so a hide test has to call `renderer.render` itself rather than read what
the loop left behind.

**THE BAKE THAT SAVED 230 DRAW CALLS TOOK EVERY WALL OUT OF TWO ROOMS, AND
THE PIXEL DIFF COULD NOT SEE IT.** `bakeStatic` takes every geometry to
non-indexed before it merges, and `buildKeepWalls` skipped any mesh with no
`index` — so the round that baked the catacombs and the tavern hall for
their draw calls left both with `S.walls.steep.length === 0`: `keepHitsWall`
never hit, `keepWallNear` answered null, the hunter's segment revert never
fired and his wall pushes pushed nothing, and the graph's 0.40 m clearance
threw nothing away. That is most of "make the creature clip through walls
less" — the walls were not there to clip. A triangle is three positions
whether or not an index names them; the index reads both now (92,777 faces
in the catacombs). **A pixel diff approves a picture; a walk approves a
room. Bake nothing without flooding the walk after it.**

**THE HUNTER WENT ROUND IN CIRCLES, AND IT WAS THE CORNER CUT.** Two rounds
of "he glitches" were measured as one thing: 78 % of roaming frames spent
in a half-metre circle — 113 m of travel in a minute, none of it anywhere —
with a live route in his hands and nothing crossing a wall. `ucFollowPath`
blends its aim toward the waypoint AFTER the current one as it closes on
it; on a route that turns back on itself (the waypoint 1.3 m west, the next
seven metres east, round the end of a wall) that aimed him AWAY from the
waypoint, the distance grew, the blend fell to nothing, he aimed back, the
distance shrank, the blend returned — a limit cycle. The next leg is blended
only when it continues AHEAD of this one. After: 0 % orbiting over four
minutes of roam, and the same follower serves the knight.

- **AND THE WALL PUSHES MUST NOT OUT-STEP THE WALK, which they did twice a
  frame.** `mutClampX` ran once from the follower and once from `catWander`
  after it, each capped at 4 cm, against a 3.2 cm stride. They run once a
  tick (`catTick`, stamped where `catPrev` is) and are capped at a third of
  the stride he actually took.
- **AND THE STRAIGHT CHASE STAYS ON YOUR STOREY.** `clear()` compared each
  sample's floor to HIS feet, which follow the floor, so a stair down beside
  you passed a riser at a time: he finished the fight 1.4 m from you in plan
  and 4.5 m under your floor, 92 % still, two swings in thirty seconds.
  Every sample must be within a step of YOUR level too; a route that keeps
  failing snaps him to the nearest node and then loses you (`catLose`); and
  four seconds still with ground to cover is a loss whatever he thinks.
  Measured after: from 35 m with a line of sight he closes to 3.9 m in
  eight seconds, four trials of four, 13–15 swings a half minute.
- **THE ROUTE PREFERS THE MIDDLE.** Every node carries `w`, its distance to
  the nearest drawn face within a metre, and A* charges nearly double for a
  node against the stone. `catLineOpen`, the string-pull and the chase's
  `clear()` test a hand either side at the hip as well as the centre line.
- **AND WHAT IS LEFT IS THE BODY.** Measured off his skinned vertices in the
  crawl: 1.65 m across the trunk, 3.3 m long, in corridors 1.3 m wide. An
  arm tuck was probed (turn the upper arms about the body's up) and bought
  8 cm — the width is the shoulders. He will touch corridor walls by
  construction; what the routing buys is that he touches both equally.

**THE WAY OUT IS LIT THROUGH THE BARS.** The door has a barred window and
the glow, the lamp and the shaft all hung above the LINTEL. Where the
window is was measured by raycasting the leaf from inside on a 10 cm grid:
the gaps between the bars run 1.7–2.2 m over the sill and from a hand left
of the door's centre to half a metre right of it. A bright unlit plate a
hand BEHIND the leaf draws the bars black against the light (drawn only
where the leaf is not, which the depth buffer does for free), a glow sits
in the opening, the lamp just inside it, and the shaft is a trapezoid from
the opening down to a pool on the flags. **A gradient down a shaft alone
is a paper cut-out** — it needs to die across as well as down, and an
edge-on quad for the side view drew as a hard line down the middle.

**HIS VOICE IS THE OWNER'S RECORDING, AND IT KNOWS WHERE HE IS.** Three
files cut into 48 cues along their own silences (ffmpeg's silencedetect at
-40 dB / 0.35 s; the steps at -38 / 0.14), sorted by length and RMS and
centroid since nobody can listen from here: the five LOUD close cues are
the roar, the six short bright ones the tell, three the hurt, seven mid
growls, four long quiet ones his breathing at a corner, the one seven-second
gutteral his feeding; twelve far growls; ten footfalls. `playSampleAt` is
the positional player — pan by bearing, level by distance, and a LOWPASS
closing with distance, which says "far" more than the level does — and
`catCue` is the one door for his voice: one cue at a time, a roar cuts
whatever is playing. The far growls come every nine to twenty-five seconds
while he is off doing his own thing beyond fourteen metres; his feet are
heard inside fifteen and nowhere else; the breath is the peek; a noise that
reaches him is always answered (growl near, far growl far). Encoded mono at
-3 dB peak, a megabyte in all. Not redistributable.

**CROUCHING IS SNEAKY.** A crouch carries three metres (was five), a walk
twelve, a sprint twenty-six — and a crouched body is harder to SEE: half
his range, a narrower cone off his line past eight metres, and he has to be
within 3.2 m to hear it whatever he faces. **AND SOMETIMES YOU SEE HIM ABOUT
HIS OWN BUSINESS**: about a quarter of his errands go to a spot you can see
from where you stand — a bone pile in view first — where he eats, sits or
looks about ABSORBED, noticing you only inside four and a half metres or by
a noise. Measured: 3 of 10 errands, 66 s of it in four minutes.

**AND THE HARNESS TRAPS OF THIS ROUND.** `bw.catG` is an OBJECT in the
original literal, so a `catG: () => catG` added to the later block is
shadowed (a later duplicate key wins — the fourth time). `bw.keepFloorAt`
is a three-argument wrapper for the keep, not the site function. A placer
that calls `startCaveIn()` every half second in dev mode re-places you every
half second, and the real loop runs between tool calls: freeze rAF the frame
the room takes. A metric that reads 0 on every frame is a metric to test
against a wall before believing it — the body probe read 0 because there
were no walls, and would have gone on reading 0 for ever.

**"HE GOT STUCK ON THE TOMBS" WAS THREE THINGS, AND ONLY THE FIRST WAS A
TOMB.** The owner played the catacombs again: the monster stuck, on the
sarcophagi, and his sounds heard from too far off. Measured by chasing the
player into the crypt room six times from 14–34 m and reading his height
against the player's floor at the end of each:

- **THE LID WAS A STEP.** `catStand` takes any storey up to 1.05 m over him
  and a sarcophagus is a metre tall, so pressed against one in a fight he
  was lifted onto its lid — 0.49 and 0.86 m over your floor at the end of
  two chases in six — and stood there 2.5 m from you, "in reach", swinging
  at the stone between. Two rules: a rise over half a metre is climbed only
  where his ROUTE goes up (a stair's riser is on the route; a lid never is),
  and a too-high storey is a HOLD, not a hole — nulling it sent him down the
  "nothing under me" branch, which sinks, snaps to a node and DROPS THE
  ROUTE, and that was a fresh stall wherever a lookup happened to return a
  lid. And a route in hand means the straight line is shut, so "in reach"
  with a route is not in reach: he walks it round the tomb rather than
  standing at it. After: never more than 0.31 m over your floor in twelve
  chases.
- **THE ROUTE BEGAN ACROSS THE WALL BESIDE HIM.** Nodes are 0.6 m apart and a
  wall is 0.2 m of stone with 0.4 m of clearance either side, so the nearest
  node to a body a hand from a wall is as likely as not on the far side of
  it — and the route's first leg then runs through the stone: traced, a
  stalk with a ten-waypoint route whose first waypoint was 6.6 m away through
  the wall he faced, the step ahead crossing at hip, shoulder and both
  sides, held there until the progress check drew the same route again.
  `catStartNode` takes the nearest node within a metre and a half that HIS
  OWN LINE reaches; the "drop the first waypoint underfoot" shift asks the
  same question; and a route he has been held against stone on for half a
  second (`catBlockT`) is dropped for one drawn from where he actually is.
- **AND A THIRD OF THE GRAPH WAS POCKETS.** 5,910 nodes in EIGHTY-EIGHT
  components, the largest 4,021: every floored ledge the packer sampled that
  nothing joins to is a component of a few dozen nodes, and a body in one
  can route nowhere. Traced: a pocket of NINETEEN nodes thirteen metres from
  the player, him seeing them the whole time, every route refused, stalk,
  chase and search taking turns at failing for twenty-five seconds. The
  largest component is the graph now — `catNodeAt` answers nothing else, so
  a snap, a target and a corner to watch from are all on it — the straight
  chase may DROP a ledge toward you (a floor up to 1.2 m below his feet is
  a fall, not a wall), and a body found in a pocket is put back on the main
  floor the moment you are not looking at it (`catUnpocket`). Started on
  that very ledge three times, he closes to 1.4–2.5 m in all three.

Measured at the end, hands-off: **six chases of six close to 1.9–2.5 m with
7–13 swings a half minute and zero stalls; three from the stranding ledge
close too; five roams of five with zero route-in-hand stalls at 1.1–2.9 m/s;
and he never rises above 0.31 m over your floor.**

**AND HIS SOUNDS ARE CLOSE-RANGE ONLY.** The owner's word: only when he is
near. Every cue caps at `CAT_HEAR_FAR` (26 m; the roar six more): the
"far" growls are the ones for the next room over, twelve to twenty-six
metres, dull through the stone, and past that he is silent — so hearing
anything of him at all means he is near.

**THE HARNESS: THE ROOM BUILDS ON FRAMES, AND A HIDDEN PANE HAS NONE.** The
cave-in's dev-mode shortcut places you only once `catReady`, and the parse
chain that makes it ready wants a frame per step: a hidden pane runs no
frames, so a placer that calls `startCaveIn()` every half second waits for
ever at x = 8. Drive frames by hand (`bw.animate()`) until `CAT_SITE.walls`
exists, then `placeInCatacombs()` directly — and `bw.catFloorAt` is the
site's floor lookup, because `bw.keepFloorAt` is the keep's three-argument
wrapper and answers null for everything here.

**THE FOG CULL'S STAMP SURVIVED THE WARM, AND THAT PUT THE HALL'S CAST IN
THE MIDDLE OF THE ROOM.** "The ufo enemies are seen in the middle upon being
abducted" — the three guards and the beast, standing at their build spot at
the centre of the hall before any wave had been summoned. Traced with a
setter on `visible`: every one of them was switched on by `cullBeyondFog`,
whose restore branch reads `bwCulled` — "I hid this, so I may show it". The
stamp was put there by the WARM: `warmView` and `warmCompile` switch the
groups they are warming on, `warmAtZ` then runs `updateFarProps` for the
pass, and from the beach a creature parked three thousand metres away is
beyond the fog — so the cull hid it and stamped it, the warm restored
`visible = false`, and the stamp stayed. Arrive in the hall, the unit is in
range, the cull "restores" it. `snapCullStamp` / `restoreCullStamp` carry
`bwCulled` through both warms beside the visibility. **Anything a warm
toggles, it has to put back in FULL — the cull's own bookkeeping included.**
Measured after: the abduction lands with all nine hidden and no stamps; the
summon still reveals the three across the room.

**A WORN RING WAS IN NEITHER LIST THE RESTORE READS.** `pack` is the
inventory and `wearRing` takes a ring OUT of the inventory, so the one item
the save recorded as `worn` was granted by nobody: it came back only if its
own pickup replayed, and the ring's pickup is registered by `dropRing` when
the knight dies — on a fresh page nothing has died, the interactable does not
exist, and the ring the owner had on his finger was gone. `finishRestore`
grants a worn name through `packByName` and puts it straight on (or into the
pack if the fingers are full). Measured: worn, saved, reloaded into the
checkpoint — on the finger on the first frame.

**THE KATANA BY THE DRAIN IS GONE.** It lay past the drainage tunnel home
from the day the sword went in; once the dojo's stand handed out the same
item there were two katanas and the first was free. Nothing is added to the
scene or registered there now; `katanaWorld` stays a group, dev mode still
hands the sword over, and an old save that recorded "Take the katana#1" finds
no handler and is granted the item by name.

**THE SLOPES SHOOK BECAUSE THE GRID IS TREADS.** "A slight lag and camera
shake walking up slanted corridors in the catacombs": the walk grid is a
plan of 0.2 m cells each carrying ONE floor height, so a slanted corridor is
a staircase of twenty-centimetre treads however smooth the stone drawn over
it, and the camera followed the treads — snapped up a riser every fifth of a
metre going up, dropped one under gravity coming down. Measured on a
hands-off walk from the landing to the door: 87 ticks with the camera moving
more than 4.5 cm in a tick and 19 over 9 cm, worst 24 cm. `catFloorSmooth`
blends the cell under the player toward its neighbours by where inside the
cell the player stands — a linear ramp through the cell centres — and only
toward a neighbour whose floor is within a step, so a real ledge stays a
ledge; the roof rides the same blend, or the duck under it stair-steps up a
ramp. It is the floor the CAMERA follows; every legality test still reads
the raw cell. After: 0 ticks over 9 cm, worst 8 cm, and the rate itself
changes by more than 3 cm on 8 ticks in 3000.

**THE HUNTER HAS A PLAN NOW: FOUR THINGS, ALL ON MACHINERY HE ALREADY HAD.**
- **HE LEARNS YOUR ROUTE.** `catMemory` is the last three places he laid
  eyes on you (both sight paths write it, six metres apart or it is the same
  place); when he has gone twelve seconds without you, two errands in five
  go to one of them — most recent likeliest — and he WAITS there (`ambush`,
  or a look or a sit). A player who runs the same corridor every time finds
  him in it. Measured: 10 of 40 errands to a remembered spot 13 m away.
- **THE FAKE-OUT.** Once a stalk, two peeks in five are a FEINT: he shows
  for a second or two, and if you have not looked, withdraws — and the next
  corner he takes is at least seventy degrees round you (`avoidA`, held
  until a corner is FOUND there: cleared after the first search it was gone
  on the retry, and he came back on the same bearing). A feint does not count
  as one of his three corners. Measured: a 2.3 s show at 12 s of a stalk,
  gone, and the next corner across the room.
- **AMBUSH AT THE DOOR.** Inside twenty metres of the way out on its storey,
  three times in five and not twice in fifty seconds, his errand is a spot
  in the door room your line cannot see, within seven metres of the frame,
  where he crouches and waits at his full senses — so the exit is not free.
  Measured with the player 9 m from the door: 15 of 20 draws, all hidden.
- **HE KICKS THE BONES AT YOU.** Charging through a pile (the litter check's
  own spots) at over 2.2 m/s with you 3.5–16 m off, he throws five to eight
  real gibs in the skulls' own material at where you stand, arcing to arrive
  in about a second, every six to nine seconds at most; one that reaches
  you takes 0.09 of the bar and knocks the lens (`catBonesHit`, in the
  room's own update). Measured at 7 m: eight of twenty-four land on a
  standing player, a volley about a quarter of the bar. It is the one ranged
  thing he has, and it is readable: stay off the piles.
Every one of them is a branch of `catPickTarget` or the stalk and touches
nothing about how he moves, so the six-of-six chases and the zero-stall roams
of the round before still hold.

**`node --check` DOES NOT CHECK THIS FILE, AND HAS NOT FOR A LONG TIME.** The
ritual at the end of every round here is `node --check main.js`, and it passed
a file with `color: 0xb0a characters` sitting in the middle of a function —
reproduced on a copy, exit 0, twice. In the CommonJS goal the whole source is
wrapped in one function and V8 PRE-parses a body that large rather than
parsing it, so an error inside a function is not found until that function is
first called; on a 200 KB fragment of the same file it is caught immediately,
and `--no-lazy` does not help. The file is a MODULE — that is how `index.html`
loads it — and as a module the check is eager:

```bash
node --input-type=module --check < main.js
```

Broken, that exits 1; clean, 0. Use it, and remember that a shell pipeline's
`$?` is the LAST command's, so `node --check x | tail` always reports 0.

**AND THE SHELF IS BACK, ON THE ONE STEP NOTHING CAN CLIMB.** A bracketed
board hung between the stall's roof and the vaulted passage once and was taken
out on the owner's word, because the file's own crate climbs that step. This
is a different wall: the back of the gallery, where the floor reads 5.30 over
the flags and the landing in front of the bore 7.42. A jump lifts the feet
0.62 and the walk catches a floor `TAV_AIR` (0.72) over them, so 1.34 is the
tallest step in that building and this one is **2.12** — the plank was the
only way in. Halfway up it splits into two jumps of 1.06, which is the rung
the crates already prove.

- **NOTHING ABOUT IT IS TYPED.** The line is walked until the floor stops
  answering, the landing is asked how far it runs each way, and the face it
  hangs on is a ray. And it is walked OUT OF THE BORE, not down the hall:
  started from the gallery the first step the line meets is the one the last
  crate already climbs, and the first build hung the shelf on that one
  (measured, at (-11.50, 4.44)) — which is the wall the owner had already had
  it taken off.
- **AND SOLID IS A THICKNESS.** `KEEP_WALL_MIN` is 0.12, under which a face is
  a sliver the wall index drops, so a 55 mm board is a floor on top and open
  air from the side and you stand inside your own shelf. The apron under its
  front edge is what a shelf has anyway and is 0.13 deep, so the front stops a
  body the way a crate does — and the two rules then agree, which is what
  makes a rung work: standing, the wall band starts a step over your feet and
  the apron is in it; at the apex of a jump it starts `TAV_AIR` over them and
  the board's crown is under it, so the walk catches the floor instead of
  pushing you off the wall.
- **AND `tavCellTop` IS A RECTANGLE NOW.** A disc round a board 1.15 by 0.52
  either loses its ends or hands out floor a third of a metre in front of it,
  which is a step onto nothing.

Measured with the game's own movement, cast asleep: walk into the wall, jump,
and the feet go 5.30 → 6.36; jump again and they go 6.36 → 7.42 and walk on
into the bore. **And `inCombat()` TAKES THE JUMP AWAY** — Space is the dodge
step while anything woken is within ten metres, so the first three runs of
that test measured a player who could not jump at all, with the drunk and the
orc 6.4 m away at the bar.

**THE FORGOTTEN WEDDING RING, AND THE FIRST ENVIRONMENT MAP IN THIS GAME.**
Cécile Amstad's "Jewelery - Ring- Diamonds", at the back of the bore between
the two jars, worn for six per cent of your pace per jar of blood you carry.

- **READ THE LICENCE, NOT THE FOLDER NEXT TO IT.** Every other model here is
  CC-BY; this one is Sketchfab Standard, and the credit was written wrong
  before the `license.txt` was opened.
- **AND READ EVERY MAP BEFORE DECIDING WHAT THE MODEL NEEDS.** Measured: all
  five of its baseColour maps are PURE WHITE and all four normal maps are
  FLAT — sixteen 4096s, a quarter of a gigabyte, of which the only content is
  five metallic-roughness maps and two emissives on the stones. They are all
  kept anyway (2.00 MB at 2048/1024, an rms of 0.9 of 255 against the
  originals): the white and the flat cost 130 KB, which is less than the
  argument about whether they are the artist's textures.
- **METALNESS IS A TRAP — the seventh time, and the first time the answer is
  not to change the metal.** Every material here is metalness 1, which is what
  a ring IS, and a metal has no diffuse term: shipped as authored the band
  rendered as a black hoop with two pale bands where the view model's own
  directionals strike. What a jewellery viewer shows it against is an
  ENVIRONMENT. `ringEnv()` is 128 by 64 pixels of this beach's night — sky,
  ground and the moon where `MOON_DIR` says it is — through three's PMREM, set
  on this ring's materials and nothing else, so the model and its maps are
  still exactly the ones in the file. `envMapIntensity` was swept: 1.6 is
  still a dark hoop, 4.2 reads as metal face-on.
- **AND `ITEM_MAX_BOOST` IS 3.2, SO THE FITTED SIZE IS THE SIZE.**
  `ITEM_MIN_SIZE` (0.42) is a floor every takeable gets, and it cannot reach a
  true-size ring from 21 mm — measured in the bore, that is two pixels at two
  metres and the glint is the only thing you could ever find. Fitted at the
  octopus ring's own 0.055 it comes out at 0.195 on the floor, which is what a
  takeable looks like here.
- **AND `makeNoticeable` GIVES UP AFTER SIX TRIES.** It measures the group and
  retries for 5.4 s, so a 2 MB model that lands after the cut into the room is
  a ring left at true size for the rest of that game — a race between a
  download and a doorway. `dropWedRing` waits for the model instead.
- **AND THE PACE YOU WALK AT HAS A DOOR NOW.** `speedK`, beside `stamMax`: the
  one place the player's speed is worked out multiplies by it, so an item can
  change it. Measured on open sand, 100 ticks to terminal speed then 60 more:
  4.76 m/s with no ring and 4.76 with four jars and no ring, 5.90 wearing it —
  +24.0 %, which is four times six.

**A SCREENSHOT OF A PANE WITH rAF STUBBED IS ALWAYS THE OLD FRAME.** This file
already says to freeze the loop for a still and to screenshot in a separate
call; what it did not say is that the two together do not work. With
`requestAnimationFrame` stubbed the page never presents, so `renderer.render`
updates the drawing buffer and the compositor never shows it — a magenta
override on the object under test came back as the same black frame as before
it, which is how half an hour went on a ring that was drawing correctly all
along. Capture the canvas in the SAME call instead (`drawImage` onto a 2D
canvas, `toDataURL`), and make the result big enough that the harness writes
it to a file — a JPEG that fits inline costs 25k tokens of context to say
nothing. And **the point-light virtualiser owns every `PointLight` in the
scene**: a probe lamp added from the harness is moved to layer 2 on the next
frame and lights nothing, which reads exactly like a broken material.

**SCROLLING THROUGH YOUR THINGS WAS A FLICKER, AND IT WAS `innerHTML`.**
`renderHotbar` threw the whole strip away and built six fresh slots on every
call — and it is called on every equip, so every notch of the wheel destroyed
six nodes and six `<img>` and made six more. Three things follow from that
and all three are the "not smooth": the browser re-decodes every icon, the
0.12 s CSS transition on the selection never runs (a brand new element starts
at its final state), and the strip visibly flashes. The slots are built ONCE
and only a slot whose ITEM changed is rebuilt; everything else is a class
toggle, which is what the transition was always for. Measured: the six DOM
nodes are the same objects before and after a scroll.

**AND A WHEEL GESTURE IS NOT A COUNTER.** The old handler added `deltaY` up
to 40 and zeroed it, which threw the REMAINDER away (a slow trackpad drag
stepped unevenly), let a flick step as fast as the events arrived (a trackpad
sends a hundred small deltas in a burst — measured, that is five slots in one
gesture), and kept a stalled gesture's half-step for ever. It keeps the
remainder, starts clean after 400 ms, and will not step more than once every
85 ms. Measured: four notches step four slots; a forty-event flick steps ONE.

**THE JARS ARE A NUMBER, NOT A THING YOU CARRY.** They had a stacking slot in
the pack with a badge on it, and the owner's word is the corner and nowhere
else — which is right: a jar is not held, equipped or used, and two places
showing the same tally is one of them lying the first time they disagree.
`gainJar` no longer adds it, and a save from before this is cleaned up on the
way through.

**AND A PILE OF BONES BREAKS.** Running through one has clattered and carried
twenty-six metres since the bones went in; a BLADE through one did nothing at
all, which is the wrong way round — it is the one noise down there you make on
purpose. The pile is triangles inside the room's own merged mesh and cannot be
taken away, so what breaks is what was lying loose on it: `catBoneStrike` is
another door in `digImpact`'s own chain (after the castle, the crate and the
glass), it throws real gibs in the skulls' material down the swing, and the
noise is registered AT THE PILE rather than at you. Measured: a swing at a
pile two metres off throws twelve bones and sets his noise at r = 26.

**THE TAVERN CAN ALWAYS LET GO OF YOU.** "I got stuck in these spots" was the
stall, and every line of the walk above it is a REFUSAL — the move is turned,
or reverted, or pushed out of — which is the Dealer's own lesson that
reverting the frame IS the stuck. Measured over the whole hall: 4,351
standable spots, 16 of them with drawn stone across all eight directions and
797 with stone a full body-radius inside the body. `tavEscape` runs LAST in
`updateTavern` and only when the body really is inside something (a wall
within 0.20 of the centre) or has nothing under it: it walks out to the
nearest spot with a floor within reach and room for a body, at 0.14 m a frame
so it reads as being shouldered aside. Measured: dropped into three different
barrels, the room puts you out and you walk away; standing normally at 280
spots round the hall the mean drift is 0.067 m.

**AND THE GRID HAS TO AGREE WITH WHAT IS DRAWN, BOTH WAYS.** `fillTavHoles`
puts a storey back where the neighbours agree on a level, something is DRAWN
at it, nothing is drawn in the body band over it (that would be a barrel, and
standing inside one is the bug this would otherwise create) and a body fits.
And the prune now drops a RAISED storey with nothing drawn under it at all:
measured, 218 of 2,636 raised storeys were a step onto air.

- **AND "IS ANYTHING DRAWN HERE" IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE CELL, NOT ITS
  MIDDLE.** The first build of that rule probed the prune's own five points,
  which all sit within six centimetres of the cell centre — and deleted the
  BARREL RACK'S TOP, the rung the whole climb stands on. A 3 by 3 over the
  cell's own width answers it properly: 218 → 103, with every rung of the
  climb intact (0.22 → 1.99 → 2.48 → 3.56 → 4.59 → 5.31 → 6.36 → 7.42).

**AND DEV MODE CAN TELL YOU WHERE YOU ARE.** Two rounds of this project have
gone on working out which wall a screenshot was taken at — matching the
owner's pictures against renders of the room, which cost hours and still
ended in a question. A place in this game is three numbers and nobody could
read them. `P` in dev mode puts them on the screen: the room, the spot in the
ROOM'S own frame (which is what every constant in the file is written in),
the floor under your feet, your heading, and where the crosshair lands.
"Stand there and press P" is one line instead of an afternoon.

**A ROOF UNDER YOUR OWN FEET IS NOT A ROOF, AND IT WAS THROWING YOU OFF THE
CARPETS.** "When I walk on top of the curtains to jump across them, when I get
near the edge I lag off" is one line at the bottom of `update()`. Every
storeyed room ducks the camera under a low ceiling, and every one of them asks
for that ceiling at `groundY` — the floor you are STANDING on, or the one you
are FALLING TO. The frame the body leaves the catwalk, `groundY` stops being
